source.title: Catapult dynamics and phase transitions in quadratic nets
source.authors: David Meltzer; Min Chen; Jun-Yu Liu

record.tranche_reason: Tests full-batch gradient descent at super-critical learning rates and measures training loss in quadratic and two-layer networks, directly examining catapult dynamics in additional settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports no CIFAR-10/100 training classification-error results; its CIFAR-10 experiments use two-class data and MSE. Figure-only curves are recorded without estimating values from the plots. Cited results from other studies are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly tests V5 using full-batch gradient descent, squared loss, learning rates normalized by initial NTK stability, and loss/NTK trajectories. Its own experiments show recovery after super-critical loss growth and divergence at larger rates. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors derive sufficient conditions for super-critical convergence in quadratic and two-layer homogeneous models using weight-norm bounds, and empirically find convergence beyond some derived bounds. At larger ReLU learning rates, both weight norms and activation sparsity can increase while generalization remains good. Sparsity as an explanation for generalization is a conjecture; several generic-data arguments are heuristic, and proving ReLU convergence throughout approximately 4 ≤ ηH0 ≲ 12 remains open.
record.recipe_differences: Full-batch gradient descent and squared loss in quadratic and two-layer networks; experiments include toy datasets and two-class image datasets. The study investigates catapult dynamics and does not test classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate changes convergence and weight-norm behavior; three-layer ReLU models diverge at a lower learning rate than two-layer models. The paper also reports dataset-dependent catapult boundaries for toy and random-data experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger super-critical learning rates increase ReLU activation sparsity and can increase weight norms while generalization remains good.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large learning rates can promote activation sparsity even when parameter norms grow.

record.peer_reviewed: Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment
record.problems: The core experiments use toy models and small two-class datasets; image experiments report MSE, not classification error. Many trajectory values are available only in figures. The authors describe some multi-datapoint arguments as heuristic or conjectural and identify lack of analytic control over NTK eigenvector evolution as a limitation.
record.rows_left_out: No otherwise eligible results left out. Cited results from Lewkowycz et al. and other prior work were excluded.

untested.parts: Training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, random-label memorization, and the stated size, stopping, and regularization qualifications.
Spurious local-minimum frequencies in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Depth degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks, identity-shortcut comparisons, deep plain tanh training, and Fixup.
Comparative effects of activation-matched initialization, signal/gradient preservation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable depth.

Sustained temporal hovering of sharpness at the stability threshold while loss continues falling over extended training, and divergence from learning rates initially below the stability threshold. Final NTK eigenvalues near the threshold do not establish that complete temporal behavior.
Batch-normalization effects on speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

missing.what: NTK trajectories accompanying the loss trajectories, including significant NTK reduction in the quadratic catapult and reduction after early growth in ReLU image experiments. These directly address V5's curvature component.
Final training-loss measurements for the image experiments, separate from the early-time curves and loss-change stopping rule.

Final normalized top NTK eigenvalues: MNIST first decreases and then returns toward 2; FMNIST and CIFAR-10 finish near 2 over much of the catapult regime, with similar behavior in three-layer models. Record these as final-state measurements, not extended temporal hovering.

Super-critical convergence in pure quadratic models on random data and quadratic teacher-student data, and in quadratic models with bias on toy and teacher-student data. Include their loss and NTK results; they are eligible results despite rows_left_out asserting none.

Additional homogeneous-network results: a− = 3/4 on the toy dataset, and a− = 1/2 on random data. The latter converges up to approximately normalized rate 4, compared with 4.5 on the toy dataset, establishing a data-dependent recovery boundary.

Single-point ReLU results: recovery within the predicted range below normalized rate 4, but dead neurons and vanishing NTK near 4.5 on (x,y) = (4,2). This distinguishes a trivial finite-loss outcome from successful recovery.

Theoretical sufficient catapult ranges and larger-rate divergence bounds, with assumptions attached. Single-point guarantees and generic-data arguments have different rigor; some generic-data bounds assume approximately static NTK eigenvectors.
missing.locator: Table 1; Appendices B.1–B.4 and C.1–C.4, especially equations 60, 68, 95, 102, 124, 138, 154, 163, and 180

missing.what: Explicit larger-rate divergence results for three-layer image models, separated from their convergent conditions. The text gives a relative boundary compared with two-layer models but no exact numerical divergence threshold.

record.verdict_notes: The original limits_scope label for R6–R8 is unwarranted: V5 already allows divergence at larger learning rates. All image networks here are fully connected MLPs trained with MSE. No exact figure-only trajectory values or divergence thresholds have been inferred from extracted axis text.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels; model size, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Teacher-student local minima frequency and student-width comparison.
Plain versus residual shortcut depth comparisons, very deep plain tanh networks, and residual training without normalization.
Activation-matched initialization, Gaussian versus orthogonal initialization, and trainable depth.
Does not report sharpness hovering at a stability threshold over extended training or characterize runs that diverge from below the threshold.

source_check.notes: Observed states apply to recovering supercritical runs within the sweeps, not every control rate. Image-loss values and exact divergence boundaries remain figure-only; the loss-change stopping rule alone does not establish low loss.
